review_text: Exceptional service from beginning to the end! My Darling MIL had a taste for meat pie and wanted to get some for the travel back home and when we walked in we were greeted with smiling faces and generosity. The meat pie took a while but the employees wanted for us to be satisfied, which to me was pretty damn awesome in my book... The fish roll, Fish pie, and meat pie were all on point and hot right out the oven YESSSS! Felt like a winner!   If you are ever in the area and have a taste for Nigerian snacks try this spot! I don't mind traveling from the north side for their food!

This review is more for Wazobia Kitchen that is next door. The market itself is fine, well stocked and clean.  Wanted some food and thought let me try the kitchen. It's a cafeteria style set up. I had jollof rice with tripe. The young man helping me, goodness I wish I remembered his name was very courteous and patient. He answered all the questions I had. Made suggestions etc...the staff welcoming and kind was adequately staffed to help everyone, no long lines. My food was great and I am ABSOLUTELY going back and have controlled myself not to go back this week. Another point I want to make is the cleanliness of the place. Good job. Do I recommended it? YES!

I cannot say enough good things about the food at Wazobia Kitchen. The flavors are consistently awesome and truly capture that authentic taste I'm always looking for. Every dish is prepared with such care, and you can really tell the difference in the quality.  I have already started telling everyone about this place! I will definitely continue to recommend Wazobia to all my friends and colleagues looking for a great meal. If you haven't tried them yet, you are missing out!

Wazobia is a consistent African kitchen I enjoy going to. I have never had anything I dislike from here. The coconut rice is probably my favorite but if you cannot tolerate spice please be careful  their jollof rice, meat pie, puff puff and designer stew are also staples of mine. Very clean and fast service. I will always come here

Your employees WILL be the reason why there will be a lawsuit against this store. Where in the store does it states pregnant women or with children will be attended to first regardless of the pick a number procedure in the meat department? So I was already waiting 9 plus minutes, so because this woman is pregnant the rules and policy for requesting for meat/poultry is voided out. That's discrimination. The sad case is they catered to the alleged pregnant woman when there should have been structure and procedure in a multi business establishment. If you're not able to do that at Walmart, HEB, or other shopping stores why would it be done at this store?

This place was the most sweetest restaurant I have ever came across!! Me and my bf were about to leave, but the sweetest lady told us to come, despite us coming 10 minutes before they closed. The employees were all welcoming and the sweetest lady was also very helpful given that it was our first time there. Idk what's up with these bad reviews but I had a great experience!!! But the only thing that disappointed me was that there was no tip button :( Will definitely be carrying cash the next time I go there!!
Customer service was bad and was so rude and she threw the food at me and the ambiance was so bad

They are terrible in Customer Service. The ladies that work there do not greet or welcome you. They are not friendly at all. The food needs improvement too. The jollof rice is too bland and not tasty.

i bought some smoked turkey from Wazobia market last week prior to stormy weather only for it to mess up my soup and stew. I discovered turkey was messed up. pls observe your meat and produce to make safe prior to service. I've been a customer for many years but this is not acceptable.

When did Wazobia start cheating its customers? Their entrees now come with just one piece of meat, and if you're unlucky, that piece of meat is either half bone or half skin and fat. The portion sizes are not worth the price ($22 for jollof rice and one ridiculous piece of meat). Too bad that they've decided to take this approach. I will be ordering from their competitor next time. Their competitor provides a side of veggies and plantains.
This store has unique offerings. Hard to fine spices and herbs, such as kola nuts can be found at this store.

My family came here and all ordered different food so we could taste as much as possible. Together we ordered fried rice with goat meat, jollof rice with goat meat, beans with goat meat, and pounded yam and egusi soup. We also wanted moi moi but they were out. The fried rice was a 10, very flavorful and the goat meat was good too. Everything else could've used more salt. I had to wait about 20 mins for the pounded yam but it came out fresh and hot. The egusi soup could've had less oil though. In terms of the ambience, they had plenty of seating and it was a clean space. My only complaint regarding dining in was the noise level. The workers don't seem to have inside voices when they're having their side discussions. Very loud talking and laughing most of the time that we were sitting down, which made it difficult for us to even hear ourselves. Overall, I wouldn't return because the food to me wasn't anything special.

They cook with love at this place. The food is tasty and filling, and makes you feel at home. The service is super fast and Stella and Ella will provide any recommendation you need. I'm a repeat customer and you should be too!

Before I begin I would like to say that this review is based solely upon my personal experiences and my personal experiences alone, so with that being said let's go!!... My brother in law ordered a few items from the kitchen side of this business for thanksgiving. We went to pick it up on the day of. There was a tent outside in the parking lot so you didn't have to wait in the cold on this particular day because it was quite breezy and chilly. But it was in the 80's the day prior to that! Weather can be unpredictable anywhere!.  There were people coming pulling up nonstop picking up food orders while we waited. When we got there my brother in law gave his name and after a while they brought his order out.  We went inside briefly to see what they had already cooked for purchase to grab something to eat while we waited.  This was the first time I had African food so he wanted me to try out something. They did not have the item he wanted me to try. But when we got back and ate the two dishes I tried was tasty. I believe it was beef kabobs on skewers and Joliff rice that was smoked and it was delicious!  I would definitely return to try other dishes on my next visit.
very good food. I haven't had a bad experience so far. I normally come here do grab some Nigerian food when I'm in the area.

The service is terrible and you will wait and wait and WAIT AND WAIT AND WAIT EH! The food is good but not worth the demeanor and behavior of the staff. The lack proper structure and process to manage the customers

Wazobia, you guys are a joke. You have the audacity to charge $23.79 for a plate of rice only to get protein that's fit for a bird! The greed is unreal. The only good thing is that you guys open on Mondays.
The food is good . The public relationship of the restaurant staff is excellent. Deliverance is on time too.

Thieves! Thieves! Thieves! They weighed my meat in the box and tried to charge me for the weight of the box and plastic that the meat comes in. They minced my oxtail and refused to replace it. HENRY is a crooked and is not customer service oriented.   DO NOT SHOP HERE!

The supermarket was well kept, clean and organized unlike many African markets in the East Coast. There was a "hot food" section which allows customers to pick food themselves which may be a food safety concern because some food cases were left open and some items looks picked through. I was going to try the scotch egg and realized that the case that it was in was pretty cold. I went next door to the restaurant portion and they had hot scotch eggs but it had no flavor. I would only visit the market for the plentiful grocery options but not the hot food.

I love eating Nigerian food. The Jollof Rice is by far the best rice I've ever tasted. The rice is full of flavor with just the rice spice. The Red Stew is so good and definitely a favorite of mines. The restaurant is very small but cute. They have a small sit down area as well. The customer service is good as well.

I live near this location and have visited multiple times. I gave them numerous chances they are just too inconsistent. I watched the server intentionally select the pictured beef meat. There was no meat on the steamtable and she went to get more and returned with this burnt mess! Sometimes the food is overcooked, burnt and sometimes it's good and fresh. They are too inconsistent for me!
The kitchen staff need to manage their time well. They need to make sure that they meet up with the pick up time. I almost rejected the food I ordered due to poor time managemen.
Best place to get a essence of Africa! And the food is good in fact I'm going now. It's also a market so u can buy your African groceries here like red palm oil and digestive biscuits hahaha

SO! my 5 stars is for the store, customer service is AMAZING, they are so sweet and make you want to go back (very polite). Food is on point, wish every Nigerian establishment would have people as polite as these guys. HOWEVER!!! The Kitchen OMG ppl are not cheerful, it's like they don't want to be there; the difference is so clear (but the food is great!). Cos I absolutely love the store they get 5 stars :)
i was their for a plate of jelof rice but ended up buying mor because of the pretty ass server and her calmness. she made my visitation good. i forgot her name but she is cool.

I pop into Wazobia for ready-to-eat food and snacks. Their jollof rice was incredible until today. I don't know what happened, but this is not the rice I can't wait to rush home and devour. For this jollof rice, I can wait for a tasty one.
Love this market! I will always make a point to visit when I'm in town. Missing the fried rice already.

The absolute, hands-down, worst service ever!! My husband called in an order, having been on the phone for greater than 10 minutes, for me to get there for pickup and be told an order was never placed. I offered the young lady attending me to speak with him via phone and was met with an impatient attitude as if she were not being paid to be there. What I find simply amazing is the fact that if a white patron came in they would likely roll out the red carpet, yet they treat their loyal customers like trash. Well, guess what, that one visit a year from a white patron cannot pay your bills! Never again will I patronize this business, as this is the second time I have been met with such disrespect, disorganization, and rudeness!! By the way, I get home to find one of the plantains we ordered already had a bite in it, see picture below. Neither I, nor our daughter, opened any of the containers before getting home.

Well never order from Wazobia again they're not consistent fish is always cold and old and when you wait they pretend they're going cook fresh fish pull off and it's the same fish . Tried to complain to manger and the woman would not connect pretended to put me on hold and kept hanging up . My colleagues have experienced the same behavior so as a collective we've decided to take them out of our lunch pool and will no longer order personally. We see opting fir Naeto's and Michelle's ! Learn how to treat people with quality service and food because you've lost a big business with my colleagues and family !!!

Wazobia in its current iteration disappoints as with a host of other foreign businesses that doesn't incentivize customer loyalty after finding success. Most restaurants entertain reasonable customer requests or propose some kind of compromise inline with the ancient principle of customer satisfaction. As with most food items, customers might prefer unique variations and Wazobia at its inception took this into account, which probably formed the premise of the success they now enjoy. Now, their policy is - "my way or the highway, if you don't want it, others will" - an attitude that alienates even the most loyal of customers, especially Nigerian folks, who try to support community owned businesses. I will not return to Wazobia after 6 years of almost weekly patronage, and this pains me tremendously.

This food was so disgusting. The jollof rice tasted burnt and had no flavor and the oha soup was thick and bland there was only 1 piece of chicken, cow tongue, and tripe. I am a cook and know how to cook jollof rice and have been to Lagos so I know what it's supposed to taste like. When I asked for a refund they told me they don't allow refunds. By law they must have a sign that says NO REFUNDS but they didn't so I WILL NEVER come back here.

5/5. Drove 35 minutes for my craving for Egusi, and they did not fail me. Walked right in, and was greeted with a smile and a lovely aroma of delicious food. I ordered goat egusi, and got fufu (they also have amala, eba and other choices). I got my food to go, and was happy to find that when I got home from another 35 minute drive, and my egusi was still piping hot, and my fufu still steaming and fresh. Would 10/10 recommend this location if you're craving delicious Nigerian food.

Never order their Catered Fried Rice. I cater from them often for parties for parties and I've never had a compliant as I am a very easy customer to please.  However, last week I ordered their friend rice for the first time, by the time I took it out of the refrigerator the next day to dish it, the rice was slippery (basically spoilt). I called the restaurant immediately, and after several attempt to tell me it was not their fault, they finally called me back 2 days later to offer me a 50% refund for food I was not able to use for the party.  Needless to say I was very upset and disappointed.  At the end of the day it is more about principle of the matter, than the money it self.  What does it cost the restaurant to give a customer their refund for a product that was damaged,  especially from a regular customer who's never had a compliant.

I have tried a lot of different things in the kitchen. Although I have only been to the one on beechnut. The one thing I love from them is the most disappointing thing, the catfish stew with just one fish for $11, the stew is good and tasty with awesome spicy kick . The egusi is ok but no one want muscle everytime come up with a better meat combination. The efo has no taste to me so is the meat pie, fish pie is good and the beef roll is also good, scotch egg is good, stew is good but their designer stew needs work. Why would anyone pay $14.99 for nkwobi in a small bowl when i can go down the street and get a bigger bowl for 10.99. Fried fish,turkey, chicken and grilled chicken are good but no seasoning. Pepper goatmeat is good but too many bones and not enough meat. Pepper meat is good. Tried the jollof rice and it was blend, goatmeat pepper is ok, catfish pepper has one fish.

Better than expected. Had heard about this place from a coworker. I looked their website up and was surprised the kitchen offers online ordering. I placed my order and received an immediate text then a follow-up confirmation call. Very pleased at how tech savvy they are. Ease of ordering was great, customer service was good.   SO on to the food....  When picking up an online order, GO TO THE KITCHEN NEXT DOOR, not the grocery market. Even though the grocery market has a snack bar area, that is not where you pick up your food. If I hadn't asked, I would have continued standing around for nothing but the market snack bar had: small jollof rice plates packaged in an aluminum container with plastic lid, scotch eggs, some meat pies and I think I remember seeing sausage rolls. All self serve. I picked up some scotch eggs which were good. I disliked the separation and thin coating of the sausage/breading because I could see the egg showing in certain places. But it still tasted good.   The market is sparse like some other reviewers had mentioned. I only needed Maggi and the cashier was kind enough to literally RUN and grab it for me because I had asked where could I find it since I missed it when I perused through the shelves. That was so kind! I think they had a bakery to the right (wasn't paying attention) as soon as you walk in, about three aisles of grocery store items, a small fresh meat deli/butcher section.  On to the food for real... I ordered a ton of food because I am impatient and my schedule doesn't allow me to drive to this location as often as I'd like. So I ordered the jollof rice plate with extra goat meat and shaki (the jollof rice plate is just the jollof so "extra" meat means adding to the rice not that they provide goat meat and shaki initially if that makes sense), meat pie (meat was too soft and the pie was too thick for my liking), chicken pie (chicken was spicy which was surprisingly good and shredded for some reason I thought it would be minced, but the chicken was dry, would have enjoyed this more if there was a dipping sauce or something), catfish pepper soup (FYI is available after 3PM), goat pepper soup and beef/sausage rolls. My favorite was the beef/sausage rolls! It is advertised on their website as a beef roll but it definitely tastes like sausage and in the description it said sausage. It is long, the crust is perfect, and I'm so glad i ordered a lot of these because I can freeze them and bring them out later. They packaged all my items WELL, nothing spilled over or made a mess when I got home and unpacked.  Even with an online order, you still have to wait in line. The line can be long and if a customer is indecisive or has a big order, yep you still have to wait. I also didn't like how customers had already placed their order/been attended to but were milling about in front of the counter as if they were waiting to be served which made it confusing if they were in line or had already been serviced but waiting for their food.  I'd support the restaurant/kitchen again.

Very rude set of workers all over. The fact is even if you are getting the food for free no one deserves that type of treatment because you will still be annoyed. Very bad customer service and rude people. Just came after years and remembered why why I stopped coming.
I prefer Southwest farmers market but this will do. They don't have as much options but again this will do
Well organized compared to some other Africa stores . Staffs are always willing and available to help . You always get to see someone around to ask for help .
This was literally the BEST Afang soup and jolly rice that I have ever eaten from any African Restaurant.I ordered via Grubnub and the food was on time and warm.Keep up the god work.Dr Flo

The best African Markets in Houston. Their food and service is consistent, the employees always greet with a smiling face. Kudos to the owner for raising the quality standard in the Diaspora food industry and really reaching out to the community. Get the food next door, it's all delicious and freshly made.  I will keep coming back!

Love this place! You can get ginormous and yummy Puff Puff for $0.50, the meat pies are large and delicious--$1.50, and the amazing Jollof Rice meals come with your choice of fish or chicken all for $4.50! I'm so happy I found this place!

This is an African food market that is adjourned to a restaurant selling food to dine in or take out. Most take out. I came here because a coworker was kind enough to share his plantain chips with me and I was instantly addicted! The taste is so much like delicious fried sweet plantain. He also told me they have good pepper soup which is so simple but my favorite Nigerian dish that I came across since I have so many Nigerian friends. The goat meat pepper soup is spicy and delicious. It's simple comfort food to me. I will be here often. Especially to get the soup through the colder months.  The market part of the establishment sells dry goods, fresh produce that is a staple in Nigerian cuisine, frozen food stuffs, beverages, and calling cards. Pretty popular place. I like it!!!
Very neat and affordable market. Though it's really far from where I stay, it was worth the drive.  The meals are fresh and very tasty.
Love the catfish stew, it's spicy and delicious at the same time. My only problem is that you'll have to buy two plates of rice to accompany the stew but it's worth it.

I don't leave reviews often but I want people to know how exceptional the service is at this store. Whenever I go to an African market the customer service is always terrible they make me feel as if I need them more than they need my service, but Wazobia is the exception! They have a great selection of grocery stuff and their restaurant is consistently good, keep it up Wazobia!
Good customer service however, the prices are very high. Paid, $12.99 for smoked fish and found same amount of smoked fish at Fiesta for $5.00.
Excellent food and good groceries. Really good food!!!!! Shish Kebob out of this world. The best Chicken and meet pies.  Really good meat rolls. Great Location.

Please watch your receipt when you shop here, this folks are thief. They will put something on the shelf for lower price, but when they scan it, the price will be double and if you are not paying attention you will pay the double price. And be also aware that they charge tax on food items, Somebody will soon call the IRS on them

This store has remained my fav for going on 2 years now. Every time my guest from out of state comes I order from the restaurant, the food delivery girl always prompt with her services. I like this place and I didn't hesitate to give it 5

Really glad I tried it out, unfortunately my taste buds did not agree with the savor. A delicacy for African tribes is a fish which they add to many of their dishes. Dishes that I tried tasted like old fish residue  (which is how they love it) but again not for me. The waitress was really nice, however, after so many questions we had she got annoyed or bothered. She did tried to cover it up and I guess it didn't kill me seeing her expression. Will not be back.
Really decent food and service. Clean location, will return for sure
My boyfriend brought me some jollof rice from here and it was soooooo freaking delicious I will be back!

Goat meat Pepper soup was absolutely delicioussss. Egusi was just ok it wasn't bad but it definitely wasn't too good and the meat was seriously lacking I asked for assorted meat and got one piece of stockfish, 1 piece of beef and a tiny piece of tendon. It was just ok but the lack of meat made me almost feel cheated , I'll go back for the goat meat pepper soup bcz it was so so so good! Never even knew such a place existed in fort bend.

As many West African and Caribbean groceries as you can imagine as well as movies, skin creams, and hot prepared Nigerian food are available here.  The hot food is DELICIOUS!!! One of my favorite snacks here is the Coconut Chips - once you take the first bite, you will not want to share it.  One unique fufu they carry here is amazing: OatWheat.  The staff is easy to talk to if you cannot find something you are looking for.
